pages.caption: Once upon a time there was a king who had many sons.
pages.description: [A grand king seated on a golden throne]
pages.scene: A grand king seated on a golden throne

pages.caption: The youngest of them could not stay quietly at home, and was determined to go out into the world and try his luck.
pages.description: [A restless prince gazing toward the horizon]
pages.scene: A restless prince gazing toward the horizon

pages.caption: After a long time the King was forced to give him leave to go.
pages.description: [A king giving his blessing at the palace gate]
pages.scene: A king giving his blessing at the palace gate

pages.caption: When he had traveled about for several days, he came to a giant's house.
pages.description: [A young prince walking a winding forest road]
pages.scene: A young prince walking a winding forest road

pages.caption: He hired himself to the giant as a servant.
pages.description: [A towering giant looming over the prince]
pages.scene: A towering giant looming over the prince

pages.caption: In the morning the giant had to go out to pasture his goats, and as he was leaving the house he told the King's son that he must clean out the stable.
pages.description: [A giant with a staff leading goats out at dawn]
pages.scene: A giant with a staff leading goats out at dawn

pages.caption: And after you have done that, he said, you need not do any more work to-day, for you have come to a kind master, and that you shall find.
pages.description: [A stern giant pointing a warning finger]
pages.scene: A stern giant pointing a warning finger

pages.caption: But what I set you to do must be done both well and thoroughly, and you must on no account go into any of the rooms which lead out of the room in which you slept last night.
pages.description: [A giant standing in a dark doorway]
pages.scene: A giant standing in a dark doorway

pages.caption: If you do, I will take your life.
pages.description: [A giant raising a threatening hand]
pages.scene: A giant raising a threatening hand

pages.caption: Well to be sure, he is an easy master, said the Prince to himself as he walked up and down the room humming and singing, for he thought there would be plenty of time left to clean out the stable.
pages.description: [A prince smirking and humming to himself]
pages.scene: A prince smirking and humming to himself

pages.caption: But it would be amusing to steal a glance into his other rooms as well, thought the Prince, for there must be something that he is afraid of my seeing, as I am not allowed to enter them.
pages.description: [A prince peering through a forbidden doorway]
pages.scene: A prince peering through a forbidden doorway

pages.caption: A cauldron was hanging from the walls; it was boiling, but the Prince could see no fire under it.
pages.description: [A copper cauldron boiling with no fire beneath]
pages.scene: A copper cauldron boiling with no fire beneath

pages.caption: I wonder what is inside it, he thought, and dipped a lock of his hair in, and the hair became just as if it were all made of copper.
pages.description: [A prince dipping his hair into the boiling cauldron]
pages.scene: A prince dipping his hair into the boiling cauldron

pages.caption: That is a nice kind of soup. If anyone were to taste that his throat would be gilded, said the youth.
pages.description: [A prince examining his copper-colored hair]
pages.scene: A prince examining his copper-colored hair

pages.caption: There, too, a cauldron was hanging from the wall, bubbling and boiling, but there was no fire under this either.
pages.description: [A silver cauldron bubbling on the wall]
pages.scene: A silver cauldron bubbling on the wall

pages.caption: I will just try what this is like too, said the Prince, thrusting another lock of his hair into it, and it came out silvered over.
pages.description: [A prince thrusting another lock of hair into the silver cauldron]
pages.scene: A prince thrusting another lock of hair into the silver cauldron

pages.caption: Such costly soup is not to be had in my father's palace, said the Prince; but everything depends on how it tastes.
pages.description: [A prince admiring his silvered hair]
pages.scene: A prince admiring his silvered hair

pages.caption: There, too, a cauldron was hanging from the wall, boiling, exactly the same as in the two other rooms.
pages.description: [A golden cauldron gleaming on the wall]
pages.scene: A golden cauldron gleaming on the wall

pages.caption: And the Prince took pleasure in trying this also, so he dipped a lock of hair in, and it came out so brightly gilded that it shone again.
pages.description: [A prince dipping a lock into the third cauldron]
pages.scene: A prince dipping a lock into the third cauldron

pages.caption: Some talk about going from bad to worse, said the Prince; but this is better and better.
pages.description: [A prince with shining golden hair]
pages.scene: A prince with shining golden hair

pages.caption: If he boils gold here, what can he boil in there? He was determined to see, and went through the door into the fourth room.
pages.description: [A prince opening a forbidden door into the fourth room]
pages.scene: A prince opening a forbidden door into the fourth room

pages.caption: No cauldron was to be seen there, but on a bench someone was seated who was like a king's daughter, and she was so beautiful that never in the Prince's life had he seen her equal.
pages.description: [A beautiful princess seated on a bench]
pages.scene: A beautiful princess seated on a bench

pages.caption: Oh! in heaven's name what are you doing here? said she who sat upon the bench.
pages.description: [A princess looking up with wide eyes]
pages.scene: A princess looking up with wide eyes

pages.caption: I took the place of servant here yesterday, said the Prince.
pages.description: [A prince bowing to the princess]
pages.scene: A prince bowing to the princess

pages.caption: May you soon have a better place, if you have come to serve here, said she.
pages.description: [A princess speaking earnestly to the prince]
pages.scene: A princess speaking earnestly to the prince

pages.caption: Oh, but I think I have got a kind master, said the Prince. He has not given me hard work to do to-day.
pages.description: [A prince smiling confidently]
pages.scene: A prince smiling confidently

pages.caption: Yes, but how will you be able to do that? she asked again. If you clean it out as other people do, ten pitchforksful will come in for every one you throw out.
pages.description: [A princess leaning forward with concern]
pages.scene: A princess leaning forward with concern

pages.caption: But I will teach you how to do it; you must turn your pitchfork upside down, and work with the handle, and then all will fly out of its own accord.
pages.description: [A princess demonstrating the pitchfork technique]
pages.scene: A princess demonstrating the pitchfork technique

pages.caption: Yes, I will attend to that, said the Prince, and stayed sitting where he was the whole day, for it was soon settled between them that they would marry each other.
pages.description: [A prince and princess sitting together on the bench]
pages.scene: A prince and princess sitting together on the bench

pages.caption: So the first day of his service with the giant did not seem long to him.
pages.description: [A prince and princess talking lovingly]
pages.scene: A prince and princess talking lovingly

pages.caption: But when evening was drawing near she said that it would now be better for him to clean out the stable before the giant came home.
pages.description: [A princess gesturing toward the stable]
pages.scene: A princess gesturing toward the stable

pages.caption: When he got there he had a fancy to try if what she had said were true, so he began to work in the same way that he had seen the stable-boys doing in his father's stables.
pages.description: [A prince working in the messy stable]
pages.scene: A prince working in the messy stable

pages.caption: But he soon saw that he must give up that, for when he had worked a very short time he had scarcely any room left to stand.
pages.description: [A prince struggling with pitchforks of manure]
pages.scene: A prince struggling with pitchforks of manure

pages.caption: So he did what the Princess had taught him, turned the pitchfork round, and worked with the handle.
pages.description: [A prince turning the pitchfork upside down]
pages.scene: A prince turning the pitchfork upside down

pages.caption: And in the twinkling of an eye the stable was as clean as if it had been scoured.
pages.description: [A perfectly clean stable gleaming]
pages.scene: A perfectly clean stable gleaming

pages.caption: When he had done that, he went back again into the room in which the giant had given him leave to stay, and there he walked backward and forward on the floor, and began to hum and sing.
pages.description: [A prince walking backward and forward humming]
pages.scene: A prince walking backward and forward humming

pages.caption: Then came the giant home with the goats.
pages.description: [A giant arriving home with his goats]
pages.scene: A giant arriving home with his goats

pages.caption: Have you cleaned the stable? asked the giant.
pages.description: [A giant with arms crossed looking skeptical]
pages.scene: A giant with arms crossed looking skeptical

pages.caption: Yes, now it is clean and sweet, master, said the King's son.
pages.description: [A prince bowing respectfully]
pages.scene: A prince bowing respectfully

pages.caption: I shall see about that, said the giant, and went round to the stable, but it was just as the Prince had said.
pages.description: [A giant inspecting the clean stable with narrowed eyes]
pages.scene: A giant inspecting the clean stable with narrowed eyes

pages.caption: You have certainly been talking to my Master-maid, for you never got that out of your own head, said the giant.
pages.description: [A giant pointing accusingly at the prince]
pages.scene: A giant pointing accusingly at the prince

pages.caption: Master-maid! What kind of a thing is that, master? said the Prince, making himself look as stupid as an ass; I should like to see that.
pages.description: [A prince looking confused and innocent]
pages.scene: A prince looking confused and innocent

pages.caption: Well, you will see her quite soon enough, said the giant.
pages.description: [A giant smirking down at the prince]
pages.scene: A giant smirking down at the prince

pages.caption: On the second morning the giant had again to go out with his goats, so he told the Prince that on that day he was to fetch home his horse.
pages.description: [A giant heading out with goats on the second morning]
pages.scene: A giant heading out with goats on the second morning

pages.caption: Which was out on the mountain-side, and when he had done that he might rest himself for the remainder of the day, for you have come to a kind master, and that you shall find.
pages.description: [A giant gesturing toward the mountain]
pages.scene: A giant gesturing toward the mountain

pages.caption: But do not go into any of the rooms that I spoke of yesterday, or I will wring your head off, said he, and then went away with his flock of goats.
pages.description: [A giant wagging a stern finger]
pages.scene: A giant wagging a stern finger

pages.caption: Yes, indeed, you are a kind master, said the Prince; but I will go in and talk to the Master-maid again, perhaps before long she may like better to be mine than yours.
pages.description: [A prince smirking as the giant departs]
pages.scene: A prince smirking as the giant departs

pages.caption: So he went to her. Then she asked him what he had to do that day.
pages.description: [A prince entering the fourth room again]
pages.scene: A prince entering the fourth room again

pages.caption: Oh! not very dangerous work, I fancy, said the King's son. I have only to go up the mountain-side after his horse.
pages.description: [A prince looking unconcerned]
pages.scene: A prince looking unconcerned

pages.caption: Well, how do you mean to set about it? asked the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid shaking her head]
pages.scene: A master-maid shaking her head

pages.caption: Oh! there is no great art in riding a horse home, said the King's son. I think I must have ridden friskier horses before now.
pages.description: [A prince shrugging casually]
pages.scene: A prince shrugging casually

pages.caption: Yes, but it is not so easy a thing as you think to ride the horse home, said the Master-maid; but I will teach you what to do.
pages.description: [A master-maid explaining the dangerous horse]
pages.scene: A master-maid explaining the dangerous horse

pages.caption: When you go near it, fire will burst out of its nostrils like flames from a pine torch.
pages.description: [A fiery horse with flames pouring from its nostrils]
pages.scene: A fiery horse with flames pouring from its nostrils

pages.caption: But be very careful, and take the bridle which is hanging by the door there, and fling the bit straight into his jaws, and then it will become so tame that you will be able to do what you like with it.
pages.description: [A master-maid handing the prince a bridle]
pages.scene: A master-maid handing the prince a bridle

pages.caption: He said he would bear this in mind, and then he again sat in there the whole day by the Master-maid, and they chatted and talked of one thing and another.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid sitting close together]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid sitting close together

pages.caption: But the first thing and the last now was, how happy and delightful it would be if they could but marry each other, and get safely away from the giant.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid dreaming of escape]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid dreaming of escape

pages.caption: And the Prince would have forgotten both the mountain-side and the horse if the Master-maid had not reminded him of them as evening drew near, and said that now it would be better if he went to fetch the horse before the giant came.
pages.description: [A master-maid reminding the prince as evening falls]
pages.scene: A master-maid reminding the prince as evening falls

pages.caption: So he did this, and took the bridle which was hanging on a crook, and strode up the mountain-side, and it was not long before he met with the horse.
pages.description: [A prince grabbing a bridle and striding uphill]
pages.scene: A prince grabbing a bridle and striding uphill

pages.caption: And fire and red flames streamed forth out of its nostrils.
pages.description: [A horse breathing fire and red flames]
pages.scene: A horse breathing fire and red flames

pages.caption: But the youth carefully watched his opportunity, and just as it was rushing at him with open jaws he threw the bit straight into its mouth.
pages.description: [A prince deftly throwing the bit into the horse's mouth]
pages.scene: A prince deftly throwing the bit into the horse's mouth

pages.caption: And the horse stood as quiet as a young lamb, and there was no difficulty at all in getting it home to the stable.
pages.description: [A gentle horse standing quiet as a lamb]
pages.scene: A gentle horse standing quiet as a lamb

pages.caption: Then the Prince went back into his room again, and began to hum and to sing.
pages.description: [A prince humming and singing in his room]
pages.scene: A prince humming and singing in his room

pages.caption: Toward evening the giant came home. Have you fetched the horse back from the mountain-side? he asked.
pages.description: [A giant asking a question at the doorway]
pages.scene: A giant asking a question at the doorway

pages.caption: That I have, master; it was an amusing horse to ride, but I rode him straight home, and put him in the stable too, said the Prince.
pages.description: [A prince gesturing proudly toward the stable]
pages.scene: A prince gesturing proudly toward the stable

pages.caption: I will see about that, said the giant, and went out to the stable, but the horse was standing there just as the Prince had said.
pages.description: [A giant examining the tame horse]
pages.scene: A giant examining the tame horse

pages.caption: You have certainly been talking with my Master-maid, for you never got that out of your own head, said the giant again.
pages.description: [A giant scowling at the prince]
pages.scene: A giant scowling at the prince

pages.caption: Yesterday, master, you talked about this Master-maid, and to-day you are talking about her again, said the Prince, who again pretended to be silly and stupid. Ah, heaven bless you, master, why will you not show me the thing?
pages.description: [A prince feigning innocent curiosity]
pages.scene: A prince feigning innocent curiosity

pages.caption: Oh! you will see her quite soon enough, said the giant.
pages.description: [A giant waving dismissively]
pages.scene: A giant waving dismissively

pages.caption: On the morning of the third day the giant again had to go into the wood with the goats.
pages.description: [A giant departing with goats on the third morning]
pages.scene: A giant departing with goats on the third morning

pages.caption: To-day you must go underground and fetch my taxes, he said to the Prince. When you have done this, you may rest for the remainder of the day, for you shall see what an easy master you have come to.
pages.description: [A giant pointing underground]
pages.scene: A giant pointing underground

pages.caption: Well, however easy a master you may be, you set me very hard work to do, thought the Prince; but I will see if I cannot find your Master-maid.
pages.description: [A prince looking thoughtful as the giant leaves]
pages.scene: A prince looking thoughtful as the giant leaves

pages.caption: So, when the Master-maid asked him what the giant had set him to do that day, he told her that he was to go underground and get the taxes.
pages.description: [A prince approaching the master-maid]
pages.scene: A prince approaching the master-maid

pages.caption: You must go to the rock there under the mountain-ridge, and take the club that is there, and knock on the rocky wall, said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid gesturing toward the mountain ridge]
pages.scene: A master-maid gesturing toward the mountain ridge

pages.caption: Then someone will come out who will sparkle with fire; you shall tell him your errand, and when he asks you how much you want to have you are to say, As much as I can carry.
pages.description: [A master-maid holding up a finger]
pages.scene: A master-maid holding up a finger

pages.caption: Yes, I will keep that in mind, said he, and then he sat there with the Master-maid the whole day, until night drew near.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid sitting together until nightfall]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid sitting together until nightfall

pages.caption: So he set out on his way, and did exactly what the Master-maid had told him. He went to the rocky wall, and took the club, and knocked on it.
pages.description: [A prince knocking on the rocky wall with a club]
pages.scene: A prince knocking on the rocky wall with a club

pages.caption: Then came one so full of sparks that they flew both out of his eyes and his nose.
pages.description: [A fiery figure emerging from the rock]
pages.scene: A fiery figure emerging from the rock

pages.caption: What do you want? said he.
pages.description: [A spark-covered figure confronting the prince]
pages.scene: A spark-covered figure confronting the prince

pages.caption: I was to come here for the giant, and demand the tax for him, said the King's son.
pages.description: [A prince standing before the fiery figure]
pages.scene: A prince standing before the fiery figure

pages.caption: How much are you to have then? said the other.
pages.description: [A fiery figure with arms crossed]
pages.scene: A fiery figure with arms crossed

pages.caption: I ask for no more than I am able to carry with me, said the Prince.
pages.description: [A prince standing tall]
pages.scene: A prince standing tall

pages.caption: It is well for you that you have not asked for a horse-load, said he who had come out of the rock. But now come in with me.
pages.description: [A fiery figure nodding approvingly]
pages.scene: A fiery figure nodding approvingly

pages.caption: This the Prince did, and what a quantity of gold and silver he saw! It was lying inside the mountain like heaps of stones in a waste place.
pages.description: [A vast hoard of gold and silver inside the mountain]
pages.scene: A vast hoard of gold and silver inside the mountain

pages.caption: And he got a load that was as large as he was able to carry, and with that he went his way.
pages.description: [A prince straining under a heavy load of gold]
pages.scene: A prince straining under a heavy load of gold

pages.caption: So in the evening, when the giant came home with the goats, the Prince went into the chamber and hummed and sang again as he had done on the other two evenings.
pages.description: [A prince humming and singing as evening falls]
pages.scene: A prince humming and singing as evening falls

pages.caption: Have you been for the tax? said the giant. Yes, that I have, master, said the Prince. Where have you put it then? said the giant again.
pages.description: [A giant pointing at a bulging bag of gold]
pages.scene: A giant pointing at a bulging bag of gold

pages.caption: The bag of gold is standing there on the bench, said the Prince.
pages.description: [A prince gesturing toward the bench]
pages.scene: A prince gesturing toward the bench

pages.caption: I will see about that, said the giant, and went away to the bench, but the bag was standing there, and it was so full that gold and silver dropped out when the giant untied the string.
pages.description: [A giant untying the bag, gold spilling out]
pages.scene: A giant untying the bag, gold spilling out

pages.caption: You have certainly been talking with my Master-maid! said the giant, and if you have I will wring your neck.
pages.description: [A giant grabbing the prince by the collar]
pages.scene: A giant grabbing the prince by the collar

pages.caption: Master-maid? said the Prince; yesterday my master talked about this Master-maid, and to-day he is talking about her again. I do wish I could see the thing myself, said he.
pages.description: [A prince looking bewildered]
pages.scene: A prince looking bewildered

pages.caption: Yes, yes, wait till to-morrow, said the giant, and then I myself will take you to her.
pages.description: [A giant grinning wickedly]
pages.scene: A giant grinning wickedly

pages.caption: Ah! master, I thank you, but you are only mocking me, said the King's son.
pages.description: [A prince bowing with false gratitude]
pages.scene: A prince bowing with false gratitude

pages.caption: Next day the giant took him to the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A giant leading the prince to the master-maid]
pages.scene: A giant leading the prince to the master-maid

pages.caption: Now you shall kill him, and boil him in the great big cauldron you know of, and when you have got the broth ready give me a call, said the giant.
pages.description: [A giant ordering the master-maid with a cruel expression]
pages.scene: A giant ordering the master-maid with a cruel expression

pages.caption: Then he lay down on the bench to sleep, and almost immediately began to snore so that it sounded like thunder among the hills.
pages.description: [A giant lying on a bench, snoring thunderously]
pages.scene: A giant lying on a bench, snoring thunderously

pages.caption: So the Master-maid took a knife, and cut the Prince's little finger, and dropped three drops of blood upon a wooden stool.
pages.description: [A master-maid cutting the prince's finger with a knife]
pages.scene: A master-maid cutting the prince's finger with a knife

pages.caption: Then she took all the old rags, and shoe-soles, and all the rubbish she could lay hands on, and put them in the cauldron.
pages.description: [A master-maid filling the cauldron with rags and shoe soles]
pages.scene: A master-maid filling the cauldron with rags and shoe soles

pages.caption: And then she filled a chest with gold dust, and a lump of salt, and a water-flask which was hanging by the door, and she also took with her a golden apple, and two gold chickens.
pages.description: [A master-maid packing a chest with treasures]
pages.scene: A master-maid packing a chest with treasures

pages.caption: And then she and the Prince went away with all the speed they could.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid fleeing hand in hand]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid fleeing hand in hand

pages.caption: And when they had gone a little way they came to the sea, and then they sailed.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid sailing a ship across the sea]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid sailing a ship across the sea

pages.caption: Now, when the giant had slept a good long time, he began to stretch himself on the bench on which he was lying.
pages.description: [A giant stretching on the bench after a long sleep]
pages.scene: A giant stretching on the bench after a long sleep

pages.caption: Will it soon boil? said he.
pages.description: [A giant calling out lazily]
pages.scene: A giant calling out lazily

pages.caption: It is just beginning, said the first drop of blood on the stool.
pages.description: [A drop of blood on the stool answering]
pages.scene: A drop of blood on the stool answering

pages.caption: So the giant lay down to sleep again, and slept for a long, long time.
pages.description: [A giant stirring restlessly on the bench]
pages.scene: A giant stirring restlessly on the bench

pages.caption: Then he began to move about a little again. Will it be ready now? said he, but he did not look up this time any more than he had done the first time, for he was still half asleep.
pages.description: [A giant half-asleep, mumbling]
pages.scene: A giant half-asleep, mumbling

pages.caption: Half done! said the second drop of blood, and the giant believed it was the Master-maid again, and turned himself on the bench, and lay down to sleep once more.
pages.description: [A second drop of blood speaking]
pages.scene: A second drop of blood speaking

pages.caption: When he had slept again for many hours, he began to move and stretch himself. Is it not done yet? said he.
pages.description: [A giant stretching again after many hours]
pages.scene: A giant stretching again after many hours

pages.caption: It is quite ready, said the third drop of blood.
pages.description: [A third drop of blood speaking]
pages.scene: A third drop of blood speaking

pages.caption: Then the giant began to sit up and rub his eyes, but he could not see who it was who had spoken to him, so he asked for the Master-maid, and called her.
pages.description: [A giant sitting up and rubbing his eyes]
pages.scene: A giant sitting up and rubbing his eyes

pages.caption: But there was no one to give him an answer.
pages.description: [A giant searching the empty room]
pages.scene: A giant searching the empty room

pages.caption: Ah! well, she has just stolen out for a little, thought the giant, and he took a spoon, and went off to the cauldron to have a taste; but there was nothing in it but shoe-soles, and rags, and such trumpery as that.
pages.description: [A giant peering into the cauldron of rags and shoe soles]
pages.scene: A giant peering into the cauldron of rags and shoe soles

pages.caption: When he saw this, he understood what had happened, and fell into such a rage that he hardly knew what he was doing.
pages.description: [A giant flying into a rage]
pages.scene: A giant flying into a rage

pages.caption: Away he went after the Prince and the Master-maid so fast that the wind whistled behind him, and it was not long before he came to the water, but he could not get over it.
pages.description: [A giant sprinting after the fleeing couple]
pages.scene: A giant sprinting after the fleeing couple

pages.caption: Well, well, I will soon find a cure for that; I have only to call my river-sucker, said the giant.
pages.description: [A giant calling out to the river]
pages.scene: A giant calling out to the river

pages.caption: So his river-sucker came and lay down, and drank one, two, three draughts, and with that the water in the sea fell so low that the giant saw the Master-maid and the Prince out on the sea in their ship.
pages.description: [A monstrous creature drinking the sea]
pages.scene: A monstrous creature drinking the sea

pages.caption: Now you must throw out the lump of salt, said the Master-maid, and the Prince did so.
pages.description: [A master-maid ordering the prince to throw the salt]
pages.scene: A master-maid ordering the prince to throw the salt

pages.caption: And it grew up into such a great high mountain right across the sea that the giant could not come over it, and the river-sucker could not drink any more water.
pages.description: [A great mountain of salt rising from the sea]
pages.scene: A great mountain of salt rising from the sea

pages.caption: Well, well, I will soon find a cure for that, said the giant, so he called to his hill-borer to come and bore through the mountain.
pages.description: [A giant calling to his hill-borer]
pages.scene: A giant calling to his hill-borer

pages.caption: But just as the hole was made, and the river-sucker was beginning to drink, the Master-maid told the Prince to throw one or two drops out of the flask.
pages.description: [A creature drilling a hole through the salt mountain]
pages.scene: A creature drilling a hole through the salt mountain

pages.caption: And when he did this the sea instantly became full of water again, and before the river-sucker could take one drink they reached the land and were in safety.
pages.description: [A sea suddenly flooding back with water]
pages.scene: A sea suddenly flooding back with water

pages.caption: So they determined to go home to the Prince's father, but the Prince would on no account permit the Master-maid to walk there.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid standing safely on shore]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid standing safely on shore

pages.caption: Wait here the least little bit of time, while I go home for the seven horses which stand in my father's stable, said he; it is not far off, and I shall not be long away, but I will not let my betrothed bride go on foot to the palace.
pages.description: [A prince insisting on fetching a coach]
pages.scene: A prince insisting on fetching a coach

pages.caption: Oh! no, do not go, for if you go home to the King's palace you will forget me, I foresee that.
pages.description: [A master-maid looking worried]
pages.scene: A master-maid looking worried

pages.caption: How could I forget you? We have suffered so much evil together, and love each other so much, said the Prince.
pages.description: [A prince placing his hand over his heart]
pages.scene: A prince placing his hand over his heart

pages.caption: But when you get there you must not even give yourself time to greet anyone, but go straight into the stable, and take the horses, and put them in the coach, and drive back as quickly as you can.
pages.description: [A master-maid giving stern instructions]
pages.scene: A master-maid giving stern instructions

pages.caption: For they will all come round about you; but you must behave just as if you did not see them, and on no account must you taste anything, for if you do it will cause great misery both to you and to me, said she; and this he promised.
pages.description: [A master-maid holding up a warning hand]
pages.scene: A master-maid holding up a warning hand

pages.caption: But when he got home to the King's palace one of his brothers was just going to be married, and the bride and all her kith and kin had come to the palace.
pages.description: [A prince arriving at a palace in the midst of a wedding]
pages.scene: A prince arriving at a palace in the midst of a wedding

pages.caption: So they all thronged round him, and questioned him about this and that, and wanted him to go in with them; but he behaved as if he did not see them, and went straight to the stable.
pages.description: [A crowd of well-wishers surrounding the prince]
pages.scene: A crowd of well-wishers surrounding the prince

pages.caption: And got out the horses and began to harness them.
pages.description: [A prince harnessing horses in the stable]
pages.scene: A prince harnessing horses in the stable

pages.caption: When they saw that they could not by any means prevail on him to go in with them, they came out to him with meat and drink, and the best of everything that they had prepared for the wedding.
pages.description: [Courtiers offering meat and drink to the prince]
pages.scene: Courtiers offering meat and drink to the prince

pages.caption: But the Prince refused to touch anything, and would do nothing but put the horses in as quickly as he could.
pages.description: [A prince refusing all food and drink]
pages.scene: A prince refusing all food and drink

pages.caption: At last, however, the bride's sister rolled an apple across the yard to him, and said, As you won't eat anything else, you may like to take a bite of that, for you must be both hungry and thirsty after your long journey.
pages.description: [A bride's sister rolling an apple across the yard]
pages.scene: A bride's sister rolling an apple across the yard

pages.caption: And he took up the apple and bit a piece out of it. But no sooner had he got the piece of apple in his mouth than he forgot the Master-maid and that he was to go back in the coach to fetch her.
pages.description: [A prince biting into the golden apple]
pages.scene: A prince biting into the golden apple

pages.caption: I think I must be mad! what do I want with this coach and horses? said he; and then he put the horses back into the stable, and went into the King's palace.
pages.description: [A prince looking confused, putting the horses back]
pages.scene: A prince looking confused, putting the horses back

pages.caption: And there it was settled that he should marry the bride's sister, who had rolled the apple to him.
pages.description: [A prince and bride's sister being united]
pages.scene: A prince and bride's sister being united

pages.caption: The Master-maid sat by the sea-shore for a long, long time, waiting for the Prince, but no Prince came.
pages.description: [A master-maid sitting alone on the seashore]
pages.scene: A master-maid sitting alone on the seashore

pages.caption: So she went away, and when she had walked a short distance she came to a little hut which stood all alone in a small wood, hard by the King's palace.
pages.description: [A master-maid walking through a small wood]
pages.scene: A master-maid walking through a small wood

pages.caption: She entered it and asked if she might be allowed to stay there. The hut belonged to an old crone, who was also an ill-tempered and malicious troll.
pages.description: [A master-maid entering a dirty, dark hut]
pages.scene: A master-maid entering a dirty, dark hut

pages.caption: At first she would not let the Master-maid remain with her; but at last, after a long time, by means of good words and good payment, she obtained leave.
pages.description: [A master-maid negotiating with the scowling old crone]
pages.scene: A master-maid negotiating with the scowling old crone

pages.caption: But the hut was as dirty and black inside as a pigsty, so the Master-maid said that she would smarten it up a little.
pages.description: [A master-maid looking at the filthy interior]
pages.scene: A master-maid looking at the filthy interior

pages.caption: She took out her chest of gold, and flung a handful of it or so into the fire, and the gold boiled up and poured out over the whole of the hut, until every part of it both inside and out was gilded.
pages.description: [A master-maid tossing gold into the fire]
pages.scene: A master-maid tossing gold into the fire

pages.caption: But when the gold began to bubble up the old hag grew so terrified that she fled as if the Evil One himself were pursuing her.
pages.description: [A gleaming golden hut glowing in the wood]
pages.scene: A gleaming golden hut glowing in the wood

pages.caption: Next morning the sheriff came traveling by there. He was greatly astonished when he saw the gold hut shining and glittering there in the copse.
pages.description: [A sheriff stopping in astonishment at the golden hut]
pages.scene: A sheriff stopping in astonishment at the golden hut

pages.caption: And he was still more astonished when he went in and caught sight of the beautiful young maiden who was sitting there; he fell in love with her at once.
pages.description: [A sheriff entering the golden hut and seeing the beautiful maiden]
pages.scene: A sheriff entering the golden hut and seeing the beautiful maiden

pages.caption: And straightway on the spot he begged her, both prettily and kindly, to marry him.
pages.description: [A sheriff kneeling before the master-maid]
pages.scene: A sheriff kneeling before the master-maid

pages.caption: Well, but have you a great deal of money? said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid examining the sheriff with a knowing look]
pages.scene: A master-maid examining the sheriff with a knowing look

pages.caption: Oh! yes; so far as that is concerned, I am not ill off, said the sheriff.
pages.description: [A sheriff proudly displaying a bag of coins]
pages.scene: A sheriff proudly displaying a bag of coins

pages.caption: But scarcely had they sat down together before the Master-maid wanted to jump up again. I have forgotten to see to the fire, she said.
pages.description: [A master-maid asking about the fire]
pages.scene: A master-maid asking about the fire

pages.caption: Why should you jump up to do that? said the sheriff; I will do that! So he jumped up, and went to the chimney in one bound.
pages.description: [A sheriff jumping toward the chimney]
pages.scene: A sheriff jumping toward the chimney

pages.caption: Just tell me when you have got hold of the shovel, said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid speaking calmly]
pages.scene: A master-maid speaking calmly

pages.caption: Well, I have hold of it now, said the sheriff.
pages.description: [A sheriff gripping the shovel]
pages.scene: A sheriff gripping the shovel

pages.caption: Then you may hold the shovel, and the shovel you, and pour red-hot coals over you, till day dawns, said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid commanding with a cold smile]
pages.scene: A master-maid commanding with a cold smile

pages.caption: So the sheriff had to stand there the whole night and pour red-hot coals over himself, and, no matter how much he cried and begged and entreated, the red-hot coals did not grow the colder for that.
pages.description: [A sheriff standing covered in red-hot coals through the night]
pages.scene: A sheriff standing covered in red-hot coals through the night

pages.caption: When the day began to dawn, and he had power to throw down the shovel, he did not stay long where he was, but ran away as fast as he possibly could.
pages.description: [A sheriff fleeing at dawn, scorched and ragged]
pages.scene: A sheriff fleeing at dawn, scorched and ragged

pages.caption: The next day the attorney came riding by the place where the Master-maid dwelt.
pages.description: [A lawyer riding toward the golden hut the next day]
pages.scene: A lawyer riding toward the golden hut the next day

pages.caption: He saw how brightly the hut shone and gleamed through the wood, and he too went into it to see who lived there, and when he entered and saw the beautiful young maiden he fell even more in love with her than the sheriff had done.
pages.description: [A lawyer entering the hut and seeing the beautiful maiden]
pages.scene: A lawyer entering the hut and seeing the beautiful maiden

pages.caption: And began to woo her at once. So the Master-maid asked him, as she had asked the sheriff, if he had a great deal of money.
pages.description: [A lawyer kneeling before the master-maid]
pages.scene: A lawyer kneeling before the master-maid

pages.caption: But suddenly she said that she had forgotten to lock the door of the porch that night, and must do it.
pages.description: [A master-maid glancing toward the porch door]
pages.scene: A master-maid glancing toward the porch door

pages.caption: Why should you do that? said the attorney; sit still, I will do it. So he was on his feet in a moment, and out in the porch.
pages.description: [A lawyer rushing to the porch]
pages.scene: A lawyer rushing to the porch

pages.caption: Tell me when you have got hold of the door-latch, said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid calling out]
pages.scene: A master-maid calling out

pages.caption: I have hold of it now, cried the attorney.
pages.description: [A lawyer gripping the door latch]
pages.scene: A lawyer gripping the door latch

pages.caption: Then you may hold the door, and the door you, and may you go between wall and wall till day dawns.
pages.description: [A master-maid delivering her curse]
pages.scene: A master-maid delivering her curse

pages.caption: What a dance the attorney had that night! He had never had such a waltz before, and he never wished to have such a dance again.
pages.description: [A lawyer trapped between the porch door and the wall]
pages.scene: A lawyer trapped between the porch door and the wall

pages.caption: As soon as the door let go its hold of him, off went the attorney. He forgot who ought to be paid off for what he had suffered, he forgot both his sack of money and his wooing.
pages.description: [A lawyer fleeing in terror at dawn]
pages.scene: A lawyer fleeing in terror at dawn

pages.caption: On the third day the bailiff came by, and he too saw the gold house in the little wood, and he too felt that he must go and see who lived there.
pages.description: [A bailiff spotting the golden hut on the third day]
pages.scene: A bailiff spotting the golden hut on the third day

pages.caption: And when he caught sight of the Master-maid he became so much in love with her that he wooed her almost before he greeted her.
pages.description: [A bailiff falling in love at first sight]
pages.scene: A bailiff falling in love at first sight

pages.caption: The Master-maid answered him as she had answered the other two, that if he had a great deal of money, she would have him.
pages.description: [A master-maid listening to the bailiff's promise]
pages.scene: A master-maid listening to the bailiff's promise

pages.caption: But hardly had they sat down together before she said that she had forgotten to bring in the calf, and must go out to put it in the byre.
pages.description: [A master-maid gesturing toward the calf outside]
pages.scene: A master-maid gesturing toward the calf outside

pages.caption: No, indeed, you shall not do that, said the bailiff; I am the one to do that. And, big and fat as he was, he went out as briskly as a boy.
pages.description: [A bailiff rushing out to grab the calf's tail]
pages.scene: A bailiff rushing out to grab the calf's tail

pages.caption: Then may you hold the calf's tail, and the calf's tail hold you, and may you go round the world together till day dawns! said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid delivering her final curse]
pages.scene: A master-maid delivering her final curse

pages.caption: So the bailiff had to bestir himself, for the calf went over rough and smooth, over hill and dale, and, the more the bailiff cried and screamed, the faster the calf went.
pages.description: [A bailiff dragged around the world by the calf]
pages.scene: A bailiff dragged around the world by the calf

pages.caption: When daylight began to appear, the bailiff was half dead; and so glad was he to leave loose of the calf's tail, that he forgot the sack of money and all else.
pages.description: [A ragged bailiff stumbling away at dawn]
pages.scene: A ragged bailiff stumbling away at dawn

pages.caption: On the following day the wedding was to take place in the King's palace, and the elder brother was to drive to church with his bride, and the brother who had been with the giant with her sister.
pages.description: [A wedding procession preparing at the palace]
pages.scene: A wedding procession preparing at the palace

pages.caption: But when they had seated themselves in the coach and were about to drive off from the palace one of the trace-pins broke, and, though they made one, two, and three to put in its place, that did not help them, for each broke in turn.
pages.description: [A trace-pin snapping in the coach]
pages.scene: A trace-pin snapping in the coach

pages.caption: Then the sheriff said, Yonder away in the thicket dwells a maiden, and if you can get her to lend you the handle of the shovel that she uses to make up her fire I know very well that it will hold fast.
pages.description: [A sheriff suggesting the shovel-handle]
pages.scene: A sheriff suggesting the shovel-handle

pages.caption: So they sent off a messenger to the thicket, and begged so prettily that they might have the loan of her shovel-handle of which the sheriff had spoken that they were not refused.
pages.description: [A messenger carrying the shovel-handle to the palace]
pages.scene: A messenger carrying the shovel-handle to the palace

pages.caption: But all at once, just as they were starting, the bottom of the coach fell in pieces.
pages.description: [A coach bottom falling to pieces]
pages.scene: A coach bottom falling to pieces

pages.caption: Then the attorney said, Away there in the thicket dwells a maiden, and if you could but get her to lend you one-half of her porch-door I am certain that it will hold together.
pages.description: [A lawyer suggesting the porch-door half]
pages.scene: A lawyer suggesting the porch-door half

pages.caption: So they again sent a messenger to the thicket, and begged so prettily for the loan of the gilded porch-door of which the attorney had told them that they got it at once.
pages.description: [A messenger carrying the gilded porch-door to the palace]
pages.scene: A messenger carrying the gilded porch-door to the palace

pages.caption: They were just setting out again, but now the horses were not able to draw the coach. They had six horses already, and now they put in eight, and then ten, and then twelve, but the more they put in, and the more the coachman whipped them, the less good it did.
pages.description: [Horses straining and the coach not moving]
pages.scene: Horses straining and the coach not moving

pages.caption: Then the bailiff spoke up and said, Out there in the gilded cottage in the thicket dwells a girl, and if you could but get her to lend you her calf I know it could draw the coach, even if it were as heavy as a mountain.
pages.description: [A bailiff suggesting the calf]
pages.scene: A bailiff suggesting the calf

pages.caption: They all thought that it was ridiculous to be drawn to church by a calf, but there was nothing else for it but to send a messenger once more, and beg as prettily as they could, on behalf of the King, that she would let them have the loan of the calf that the bailiff had told them about.
pages.description: [A messenger pleading with the master-maid for her calf]
pages.scene: A messenger pleading with the master-maid for her calf

pages.caption: Then they harnessed the calf to see if the coach would move; and away it went, over rough and smooth, over stock and stone, so that they could scarcely breathe, and sometimes they were on the ground, and sometimes up in the air.
pages.description: [A calf pulling the coach at breakneck speed]
pages.scene: A calf pulling the coach at breakneck speed

pages.caption: And when they came to the church the coach began to go round and round like a spinning-wheel, and it was with the utmost difficulty and danger that they were able to get out of the coach and into the church.
pages.description: [A coach spinning like a spinning-wheel before the church]
pages.scene: A coach spinning like a spinning-wheel before the church

pages.caption: When they had seated themselves at the table the Prince who had been in service with the giant said that he thought they ought to have invited the maiden who had lent them the shovel-handle, and the porch-door, and the calf up to the palace.
pages.description: [A prince suggesting they invite the maiden]
pages.scene: A prince suggesting they invite the maiden

pages.caption: The King also thought that this was both just and proper, so he sent five of his best men down to the gilded hut, to greet the maiden courteously from the King, and to beg her to be so good as to come up to the palace to dinner at mid-day.
pages.description: [A king sending five messengers to the golden hut]
pages.scene: A king sending five messengers to the golden hut

pages.caption: Greet the King, and tell him that, if he is too good to come to me, I am too good to come to him, replied the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid speaking with quiet dignity]
pages.scene: A master-maid speaking with quiet dignity

pages.caption: So the King had to go himself, and the Master-maid went with him immediately.
pages.description: [A king escorting the master-maid to the palace]
pages.scene: A king escorting the master-maid to the palace

pages.caption: And, as the King believed that she was more than she appeared to be, he seated her in the place of honor by the youngest bridegroom.
pages.description: [A master-maid seated in the place of honor]
pages.scene: A master-maid seated in the place of honor

pages.caption: When they had sat at the table for a short time, the Master-maid took out the cock, and the hen, and the golden apple which she had brought away with her from the giant's house, and set them on the table in front of her.
pages.description: [A master-maid placing the golden apple, cock, and hen on the table]
pages.scene: A master-maid placing the golden apple, cock, and hen on the table

pages.caption: And instantly the cock and the hen began to fight with each other for the golden apple.
pages.description: [A cock and hen fighting over the golden apple]
pages.scene: A cock and hen fighting over the golden apple

pages.caption: Oh! look how those two there are fighting for the golden apple, said the King's son.
pages.description: [A king's son watching with sudden recognition]
pages.scene: A king's son watching with sudden recognition

pages.caption: Yes, and so did we two fight to get out that time when we were in the mountain, said the Master-maid.
pages.description: [A master-maid speaking softly]
pages.scene: A master-maid speaking softly

pages.caption: So the Prince knew her again, and you may imagine how delighted he was.
pages.description: [A prince leaping up in joyful recognition]
pages.scene: A prince leaping up in joyful recognition

pages.caption: He ordered the troll-witch who had rolled the apple to him to be torn in pieces between four-and-twenty horses, so that not a bit of her was left.
pages.description: [A prince ordering justice against the troll-witch]
pages.scene: A prince ordering justice against the troll-witch

pages.caption: And then for the first time they began really to keep the wedding, and, weary as they were, the sheriff, the attorney, and the bailiff kept it up too.
pages.description: [A prince and master-maid reunited at last]
pages.scene: A prince and master-maid reunited at last
